subject: implementer
reason: The endpoint and page follow existing Catalog.API and WebApp patterns and meet the story, but the optional brand-mates call on ItemPage only catches HttpRequestException, so a timeout, open circuit or bad JSON would break a product page that worked before.

items.reason: The optional brand-mates call is wrapped in catch (HttpRequestException) only. Resilience-handler failures (TimeoutRejectedException, BrokenCircuitException, TaskCanceledException on timeout) and JsonException are not caught, so they reach the outer handler and break the whole product page. This regresses the page and contradicts the decision that a failed brand-mates call hides the section.
items.fix: Catch Exception (letting OperationCanceledException from caller cancellation propagate), log a warning, and leave brandMates empty. Make CatalogService.GetBrandMates return result ?? [] instead of result!.

items.title: Default call returns the four first other items of the brand, ordered by name, without the item itself
covers: Outputs: 200 array, never item id itself, ordered by name
items.reason: AC1 and the core rule of the endpoint (default count 4, self excluded, ordinal name order, only the same brand). It is a functional case because it is an API contract against the real database. The target item "Aardvark Target" sorts first in its brand, so a missing exclusion would show up; the lowercase name "alpha lowercase pack" would sort early under a culture or case-insensitive order, so it also guards the ordinal rule at the cut-off.

items.title: count=12 returns all six other items in ordinal name order
items.reason: AC2 and the upper boundary just inside the limit (12) when the brand has fewer items than count. Ordinal ordering is checked here with the lowercase name that must come last (uppercase letters sort before lowercase in ordinal order). Functional layer: API contract on the real database.

items.title: count=1 (lowest valid value) returns only the first other item
items.reason: Boundary just inside the lower limit of `count`: 1 must be accepted and cap the result at one item, the first by name. Without it a `count >= 1` vs `> 1` off-by-one would go unnoticed. Functional layer, same data as the other API cases.

items.title: The only item of its brand gets 200 with an empty array
covers: Outputs: empty array when the brand has no other items
items.reason: AC3: "no brand-mates" is a success, not a 404; the product page relies on an empty array to hide the section. Functional layer because it is an API status/body contract.

items.title: Unknown item id returns 404
covers: Outputs: 404 Not Found when no item has that id
items.reason: AC4: an unknown item must be distinguishable from a brand without other items (TC-CAT-1-04). Functional layer: status code contract.

items.title: count=0 (just below the lower limit) returns 400 problem details
covers: Outputs: 400 problem details when count below 1
items.reason: AC5, lower boundary just outside the limit. Functional layer: validation contract of the endpoint, including the problem details body the story requires.

items.title: count=13 (just above the upper limit) returns 400 problem details
covers: Outputs: 400 problem details when count above 12
items.reason: AC5, upper boundary just outside the limit (12 is accepted in TC-CAT-1-02). Functional layer: validation contract.

items.title: The endpoint also answers on API version 2.0
items.reason: The story states the endpoint exists in both versions 1.0 and 2.0; the other cases use 1.0. A route registered in only one version group would break the WebApp or other clients on the other. Functional layer: routing/versioning contract.

items.title: Out-of-stock brand-mates are included
covers: Open Questions: out-of-stock items are included
items.reason: The story's answered open question says out-of-stock items are returned (stock is not part of the story). A stock filter added later or by mistake would silently remove items; item 1003 "Charlie Pack" has stock 0 to detect that. Functional layer: depends on the data only.

items.title: Each returned item has the same shape and values as GET /items/{id}
covers: Outputs: same item shape as GET /api/catalog/items/{id}
items.reason: The story says the elements have the same shape as `GET /api/catalog/items/{id}` (the WebApp deserializes them as catalog items and renders cards from them). Comparing against the single-item endpoint catches missing or renamed fields. Functional layer: JSON contract.

items.title: A visitor sees "More from Brand Alpha" with four product cards on the product page
covers: Outputs: up to four product cards with picture, name, price
Outputs: section below the product details

It checks the default count of four (the brand has six others), the exclusion of the item itself, and the card content.

items.title: A signed-in shopper sees the same "More from" section
covers: AC6: shopper signed in or not
items.reason: AC6 says "signed in or not". The product page renders differently for signed-in users (for example the add-to-cart controls), so the section must be shown in that state too. E2E, same reason as TC-CAT-1-11.

items.title: Following a brand-mate card opens that item's product page

Outputs: each card links to its own product page
items.reason: AC6 last clause: the card must link to its own item, not to the current one. E2E because the navigation and the rendered target page are only visible in the browser.

items.title: The only item of its brand shows no "More from" section and the page is otherwise unchanged
covers: Outputs: when the endpoint returns no items the section, heading included, is not shown
items.reason: AC7: an empty heading or an empty box would be visible noise; the whole section must be absent while the product details still render. E2E because it concerns what the browser shows.

reason: GET brand-mates with count outside 1-12 returns 400 with content type application/json instead of application/problem+json
